expert_blurbs.author: vanekjordan
expert_blurbs.text: The Panthers have faced a wide range of QBs this season, and there's been a pretty clear trend: the bad ones have struggled, while the good ones have put up massive numbers. On a short week, Jordan Love completed 78% of his passes for 288 yards and three TDs despite Christian Watson leaving early. Bo Nix was able to attack downfield without Jaylen Waddle, and Jared Goff torched this defense for 412 passing yards. On the other hand, Carolina has also faced Tanner McKee, Cooper Rush, and a Baker Mayfield-led offense that barely threw the football. Those matchups have helped make this defense look better than it actually is against capable passing attacks. I think Shough is in an absolute smash spot here, especially with the weapons he has at his disposal.

expert_blurbs.author: Notorious
expert_blurbs.text: Apart from the Vikings game, Shough has found a way to get there every week, including 20 points last week in a game with no touchdown until the 4th quarter. He already had great weapons, and now Jordyn Tyson is in the fold. He also has sneaky rushing upside, with 20+ rushing yards in 4 of 8 games. The Saints have a healthy 24.5-point team total at home against the Panthers, who are 23rd in EPA allowed per dropback.

players.notes: Healthy 24.5 implied total. Sneaky rushing floor against weak pass defense.

expert_blurbs.author: headChopper
expert_blurbs.text: This Dallas defense has been one of the worst in the NFL this year. They've given up a ton of production through the air against just about any competent passing offense, and they've been soft in the red zone. The cherry on top here is that Brock Purdy scrambles about two and a half times per game. And if you've watched the Cowboys at all this year, you've seen numerous athletic quarterbacks absolutely gouge them on the ground.

expert_blurbs.author: Notorious
expert_blurbs.text: Purdy has been one of the most consistent quarterbacks in fantasy, with 17+ points in every game but one and three games over 26. His XFPPG says it’s sustainable, and he’s done it without many of his weapons. That receiving room is finally getting healthy, and the Cowboys are 28th in EPA allowed per dropback and 30th in schedule-adjusted fantasy points allowed to QBs.

players.notes: Elite rushing upside against Dallas, facing a weak secondary in a dome.
High implied team total and Strong rushing floor in a home matchup.
High game total and pass volume upside in a favorable dome matchup.

expert_blurbs.author: ebeimfohr
expert_blurbs.text: Lawrence can put up a strong fantasy score here even on limited volume, but if the Titans can push back at all, we might see his biggest score of the season against a terrible Titans defense.

players.notes: Strong passing volume upside as a heavy home favorite against Tennessee.

expert_blurbs.author: BobbyGomes
expert_blurbs.text: Mahomes at $6K is too cheap to pass up in small field. The Chiefs are implied for over 25 points, and they play this one in a dome against a Falcons defense that can’t get stops. He’s averaging 19 DK points a game, and his floor gets a lift from the run game opening up around him. Easy click.

players.notes: Low salary with a 25-point implied team total in a dome game.
Strong home implied team total and solid passing volume expectations.
Solid passing volume projection in a tight divisional game environment.
High game total environment with expected pass volume as an underdog.

expert_blurbs.author: headChopper
expert_blurbs.text: Hubbard has established himself as the lead back on this team, and this week Carolina takes on a New Orleans defense that has allowed the most fantasy points to running backs in the league this year. Hubbard has been a very efficient runner, and this game has the potential to turn into a high-scoring affair.

expert_blurbs.author: Notorious
expert_blurbs.text: Hubbard is a true bell cow, with 81% of the snaps and almost all of the high-value touches. He has a clear path to 20+ touches against the Saints, who are 28th in EPA against the run and 31st in schedule-adjusted fantasy points allowed to RBs.

players.notes: True Bell cow with heavy snap share and goal-line work vs. A weak rush defense.

expert_blurbs.author: BobbyGomes
expert_blurbs.text: Everyone is going to flock to the cheap Chiefs backfield, which leaves Bijan as the leverage play at RB. He’s averaging nearly 19 carries and over 4 targets a game, a workload almost no back on this slate can match. If this game turns into a shootout, the Falcons have to keep feeding him to keep pace. At $8,200 he’s a ceiling play that will be lower owned than he should be.

players.notes: Elite touch volume and high projection in a Strong game total matchup.

expert_blurbs.author: Notorious
expert_blurbs.text: CMC is my favorite spend at running back. I was worried about his hamstring last week, but he played 68% of the snaps with 20 touches and 2 touchdowns. He’s off the injury report this week and has one of the best matchups on the slate, against a Cowboys defense that is 31st in EPA against the run and 32nd in schedule-adjusted fantasy points allowed to RBs.

players.notes: High-value touch volume and explosive ceiling in a game with a 55.5 total.
Solid touch projection and favorable team total as a home favorite.
Strong game script as a heavy home favorite with heavy touch volume.

expert_blurbs.author: DavisMattek
expert_blurbs.text: Call me crazy but I want KW3 over CMC and Bijan. He is the Chiefs' target leader inside the redzone which is a very unexpected part of his game. The Chiefs get to play this game in a dome against the overmatched Falcons defense.

expert_blurbs.author: NeilCO
expert_blurbs.text: The Falcons have given up the 2nd-most schedule-adjusted fantasy points per game to running backs over the last 5 weeks. The Chiefs are heavily-favored, and Walker averages more than 30 fantasy points per game in wins this season. Walker is questionable, so monitor this situation. If he plays, Walker is a great tournament play. If Walker doesn't play, Emmett Johnson will be the best play on the slate.

players.notes: Watch for News: Walker Q - Johnson huge value if no Walker.
Strong snap share and explosive scoring ceiling in a 55.5 game total.

expert_blurbs.author: vanekjordan
expert_blurbs.text: The Colts run defense without Deforest Buckner has been horrendous. They are allowing over 4.5 yards per carry and over 1.45 yards before contact. The Dolphins will run the ball a lot with Kyle McCord at QB and this game should feature the Dolphins playing with a lead at some point.

players.notes: Solid touch floor and rushing role in a close divisional matchup.
Heavy touch volume expected as a home favorite against Miami.

expert_blurbs.author: Notorious
expert_blurbs.text: I’ve tried to make Jefferson work a few times this year, and neither Kyler Murray nor Carson Wentz (outside of the opener) was the answer. Something tells me Kirk Cousins is. The last time they played a full season together, Jefferson led the NFL in receptions and receiving yards. Plenty of teams left Cousins to the wolves and called him washed, but he had a resurgence in Las Vegas, and now he’s back in a system he knows. The Packers have been better defensively lately, but they still rank 10th-most in schedule-adjusted fantasy points allowed to WRs. T.J. Hockenson is also expected to miss, which is another reason to target Jefferson.

expert_blurbs.author: BobbyGomes
expert_blurbs.text: Jefferson’s volume is back. He’s seen 9 targets a game over his last four, and Green Bay has been one of the most generous defenses to wideouts. At $6,800 he’s the safest high-volume WR in this range. If the Vikings are short at TE, his target share only goes up.

players.notes: Averaging 9 targets per game with an expanded target share against Green Bay.

expert_blurbs.author: headChopper
expert_blurbs.text: Coker simply represents a much better value on FanDuel. This game has plenty of scoring potential, with two porous defenses that could turn it into a shootout.

expert_blurbs.author: ebeimfohr
expert_blurbs.text: The Panthers offensive line is getting healthy, and that is a huge deal for their offensive upside, especially for Coker. We are not far removed from conversations about whether Coker was actually the WR1 in Carolina and how underpriced he was on a weekly basis. The Panthers offensive line has thwarted their ability to consistently move the ball through the air, and especially in a matchup with a brutal Saints defense, I expect Coker to revert back to the incredible fantasy asset we thought he was just a few short weeks ago.

expert_blurbs.author: NeilCO
expert_blurbs.text: Coker could be $1,000 more expensive and he'd still be a great play. These are the two fastest offenses in the league in terms of seconds per play. The Saints defense has allowed the 5th-most schedule-adjusted fantasy points per game to wide receivers over the last 5 weeks. And it's a particularly juicy matchup for Coker. The Saints have played Single High coverage at the 2nd-highest rate in the league this year (64.4%). Coker averages 2.22 yards per route run against Single High, compared to 1.38 against Two High.

players.notes: Fast-paced game environment with elite production against single-high coverage.

expert_blurbs.author: vanekjordan
expert_blurbs.text: Olave saw 198 air yards last week, and now he gets a matchup where I expect the Saints to continue attacking downfield and connect on a few of those deep shots. He also has Jordyn Tyson alongside him to help carry more of the load in the passing game, which should make it tougher for defenses to focus all their attention on Olave.

players.notes: Massive air yards volume and deep target upside against Carolina.
Strong target projection in a high-paced divisional matchup.
Solid slot target projection and Price value in a dome contest.
Consistent target volume and Strong salary relief.
Strong target share and deep route participation in a high-total game.
Solid route participation and red-zone target upside in a divisional game.
Elite target volume and ceiling in a game with a massive 55.5 total.
Explosive deep route participation and high-value red-zone targets.
Clear alpha target share and Strong air yards projection.
Strong perimeter route participation in a high-scoring game environment.

expert_blurbs.author: headChopper
expert_blurbs.text: The Colts traded away a bunch of wide receivers, so there aren't many options left in the passing game these days. But even aside from all that, this DraftKings price tag represents tremendous value at the tight end position this week.

expert_blurbs.author: vanekjordan
expert_blurbs.text: He's the main target, the Dolphins funnel things underneath and it really wouldn't shock me to see him catch the ball 12 times this weekend.

expert_blurbs.author: Notorious
expert_blurbs.text: It’s tough to trust anyone on the Colts, but everything sets up for Warren. With Josh Downs and Keenan Allen gone, he’s clearly the top pass catcher. I worry about the offense as a whole, but they have a decent 21.5-point team total against the Dolphins, who are 29th in fantasy points allowed to tight ends.

expert_blurbs.author: BobbyGomes
expert_blurbs.text: Warren is getting real volume, with 8.5 targets a game over his last four. Miami has been below average at defending tight ends. At $4,400 that’s a strong floor for cash. He’s a solid, steady click.

players.notes: Averaging 8.5 targets per game with an expanded pass-catching role.

expert_blurbs.author: BobbyGomes
expert_blurbs.text: Kittle is still Purdy’s go-to target, averaging 8.5 targets over the last four. Dallas has been a sieve all year and this game should turn into a shootout. At $6,500 most of the field will save at TE and get off him. He’s the ceiling play at the position.

players.notes: Averaging 8.5 targets over his last 4 contests and is in a game with a 55.5.

expert_blurbs.author: DavisMattek
expert_blurbs.text: Give me Parkinson for dirt cheap over hoping that Tyler Warren can PPR scam for me at massive ownership.

players.notes: Cheap salary with a steady route participation.

expert_blurbs.author: NeilCO
expert_blurbs.text: Higbee has an 18.6% target share with Puka Nacua off the field this season, a bump of more than 10% from his share with Nacua. It's a strong schematic matchup, as the Cardinals play Two High at the 2nd-highest rate in the league and Higbee average 1.50 yards per route run against Two High (1.05 against Single High). And he's leverage on the Colby Parkinson chalk.

players.notes: Significant target share boost and Strong metrics against two-high coverage.
Consistent target floor and red-zone role in an indoor matchup.
Elite target volume and route participation at the tight end position.

expert_blurbs.author: ebeimfohr
expert_blurbs.text: On a weak TE slate, Strange is one of totally unowned options that can produce a big game in either yardage or with a TD or two.

players.notes: Low ownership option with big-play receiving upside on a weak slate.
Elite target share and explosive receiving ceiling in a dome game.
Strong route rate and red-zone receiving role in a divisional matchup.
Solid seam usage and target upside in a high-total game environment.
